name: Coquus AI
tag: An operating system for company workflows: shared context, AI employee skills, connected tools and human review built in.

scenarios.title: Give an AI employee a new skill
scenarios.ask: Teach our AI employee to handle supplier invoice questions. We get about {questions} a week.
steps: Linked the skill to your supplier list, payment terms and the accounting system.
Wrote the skill from 20 past answered questions: look up the invoice, check status, reply with the expected pay date.
Replayed 20 past questions. Matched your team's answer on 18.
followups: What happens on the 2 it got wrong?
Both involved disputed invoices. The skill now hands any disputed invoice to a person instead of answering.
Yes. Start with every reply reviewed, then move to spot-checks once you're comfortable with the results.

scenarios.title: Connect a workflow across tools
scenarios.ask: When a deal closes in our CRM, set up the customer in {tools} other tools and tell the team.
steps: Mapped the steps: create the account, project, billing record and kickoff meeting.
Connected {tools} tools through their standard connectors.
Passed the deal notes to every step so nobody retypes them.
A person checks the billing record before it's created.
followups: What if one tool is down?
That step waits and retries, and the team sees which deals are waiting on it. Nothing gets half-created silently.
Can we change the steps ourselves?
Yes. Workflows are edited in plain language or with a simple step list.

scenarios.title: Review queue for the team
scenarios.ask: Our AI employees produce about {items} items a day for review. Make the queue manageable for {reviewers} reviewers.
steps: Grouped items by type and risk.
Put {=round(items * 0.15)} high-risk items first, such as anything about money or contracts.
Low-risk items can be approved in batches after a quick scan.
Tracks what reviewers change and suggests skill updates weekly.
followups: Why not let it run without review?
You can for low-risk work once it's proven. Keeping people on high-risk items is how most teams stay comfortable.
Yes. Rejected items and edits feed into suggested skill updates, which a person approves.
